lines.text: Examples of discrimination: a man gets a higher salary than a woman for the same work and the same experience; colleagues make nasty jokes about a gay man; a Muslim is not allowed by his manager to pray during his break; a woman does not get the job because she is pregnant.
What can you do about discrimination?
Discrimination is forbidden by law in the Netherlands.
Everyone has the same rights in the same situation.

Steps: first talk to the person themselves; if that does not help, make an appointment with your manager/supervisor [leidinggevende]; if your manager is the one discriminating, talk to a confidential adviser [vertrouwenspersoon]; organisations such as a trade union [vakbond] can help you; and if that does not help, you can file a police report [aangifte doen] or report it to a reporting point [meldpunt] for discrimination.
